summary: Enhance your role in the C-Suite with our strategic accounting training. Learn to leverage financial insights for better decision-making and leadership.
lede: Accounting as a Strategic Partner to the C-Suite helps finance professionals connect financial statements, management accounting, forecasting, and executive decision-making. You will use FP&A practice, KPI design, variance analysis, scenario planning, and stakeholder communication to turn accounting data into clear, board-ready insight. The course develops practical skills for building variance packs, performance scorecards, executive decision briefs, and finance action plans. Through Excel-based analysis, management reporting, and leadership communication, you will learn to explain performance gaps, test assumptions, and support capital and cost decisions with credible evidence.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for finance professionals who already work with accounting data and now need to influence decision-makers. It fits people responsible for reporting, forecasting, controls, performance measurement, and executive communication across finance and business functions. Management Accountants who prepare management packs and explain business performance. Financial Controllers who review reporting quality and executive finance outputs. FP&A Analysts who build forecasts, scenarios, and performance dashboards. Finance Business Partners who advise leaders on decisions and trade-offs. Senior Accountants who need stronger strategic communication with management. Cost Accountants who analyze product, customer, and process profitability. Business Unit Finance Managers who coordinate budgets and performance reviews. Group Reporting Accountants who translate consolidated results for leadership. Audit and Risk Finance Specialists who assess reporting integrity and controls. CFO Office Analysts who support board packs and leadership briefings.
prerequisites: Bring a laptop and a working knowledge of Excel. No programming is required. Prior experience with management accounts, budgeting, or FP&A reporting will help you participate fully in the applied exercises.
